title: An Old Umbrella
subtitle: You've had it before. The silent, old and familiar black.

trails.title: Trail ① Wet Letter
trails.description: A letter with lovely stamps wet by dews.

content.text:
Dear Z, the last person from who I'd expect a letter,

I am glad to hear from you.
About what you wrote to ask, I didn't find anything. No one in the France branch knows about the "Storm," including the leader and some of the senior officers. I think you have to give up on this one.
But we need to know more about the "Storm," so do those big shots. That's why the Foundation is desperate for a source of information and values the "Timekeeper" so much. That being the case, we are back to the beginning ... How ridiculous. I don't think there is anything else I can do for you or her.
The good news is, my business trip to the France branch has been smooth, and I'm estimated to be back in the headquarters tomorrow afternoon (I'm writing this before my way back so I can use the beautiful special stamp I got here).
Maybe we can have another game by then. The people here are not good at ping-pong, so things became boring after I had beaten everyone I saw.

By the way, congratulations on your promotion.
I'm glad to know you have already adapted to the style of communication and the work in the Foundation. Clever as you are, we all know you were still thinking and acting the "scientist" way. Anyway, the time no longer goes forward, but it didn't stop. It has brought us to this mess and we have to do something.

One more thing—
keep the black umbrella you mentioned. You don't always get to find a rain gear used by someone that witnesses and braves the "Storm."

Yours,
Katz
From the France branch

items.text: El oro de los tigres
An Old Umbrella

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Vertin ...
Through the window, she sees a beam of light penetrates the statue suspended in time.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: I saw ... Vertin ... by the "Storm" ...!

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: It's just a nightmare.
The slender figure gets up. The lobby is as spacious as it used to be, but she's the only being walking across it now.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: A nightmare overly real.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Is it because I haven't seen them for so long?
Rarely this place would be in such serenity.
Since their return to the Foundation, each one of them has been invited to a one-on-one talk with the Foundation's personnel.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Vertin ... was the first to leave.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: She said she was going to talk to Madam Z about which department we would belong to. I haven't heard from her since then.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes. Here are their background reports I wrote for your perusal.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Then, Sotheby.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Her boredom was swept away by the invitation. She departed in such a haste that her beloved doll was left behind on the carpet.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: This is Sotheby. A well-educated lady born in a traditional arcanist family.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She comes from an extremely privileged background. Her family had a special influence around the world.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Besides, she has limited social skills and scientific knowledge. It will be difficult to assimilate her.

items.speaker: Druvis Ⅲ
items.text: Compared to Sotheby, Mr. APPLe was apparently not very happy to be invited. When he left, he turned a little green.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Mr. APPLe, under his modest and gentle appearance, lies a sharp perception by nature.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Being so erudite, he always has his own views of our historical intelligence.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: As far as I know, he remains upset about Captain Regulus's involuntary affiliations with the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: While Regulus has never been truly accepted by the Foundation.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: She has missed out all the education and training a member of the Foundation should have received. The influence left by the outside world on her is like a banner among the ordinary staff in the Foundation. A banner way too salient.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Once the banner was held up, new arguments were raised, and thus exacerbated the factional conflict inside the Foundation.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Factional conflict? There ought to be no factions in the Foundation. All of us share one common goal. You should know that well.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: But the conflict has been there all the time.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: And it only grows.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The group that believes in "mankind supremacy" is splitting the Foundation's belief apart.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: ... So, time isn't the only thing you've been observing these years.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The conflicts cannot be covered by regulations anymore, Madam Z.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The "Storm" has been here for 8 years. None of the people who are left behind can shake off the influence it brought.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Human technologies are being reversed, while arcanum is blooming.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The unexpected first "Storm" brought more than half of the Foundation's elite members away from us. The number of staff of the House of Integratus and the Committee cannot compare with that of their heyday even now.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: In order to contend against Manus Vindictae, we have kept absorbing arcanists from the outside world ... However, the dissenting voices have only grown louder ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Loud enough to be heard, and have become a faction that couldn't be shaken—the Mankind Caucus.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Beyond their control, these new arcanists only brought fear. They demand an unchallengeable power to make decisions and a harsher control of arcanists.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Madam Z, I don't want my friends or me to be the sacrifice of this conflict ... As we were four years ago.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: That's why you handed in the background reports of those arcanists as the evidence for your proposition in the negotiation.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Vertin, what do you want?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: A neutral, safe, and legitimate place for us.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: What if I'm also on the side of Mankind Caucus?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I don't know whose side you are on. But I believe the future you pursue doesn't end up with the Foundation being split apart by factional conflict.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That's what I learnt from that stormy night.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Your eyes told me ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... you didn't belong to that chess game.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: ... You may leave the reports. I need some time.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: No matter what your decision is ... thank you.
In the middle of the office stands solely the lady in white.
She flips through the files, sighs, and then picks up the phone.

items.speaker: Z
items.text: Please put me through Delegate Mark.
The long hallway is located between the Committee and the House of Integratus, forming a bridge between the two loci of power.
Familiar and unfamiliar ones bustle around in the hallway, holding proposals that only have a one-in-ten chance of passing.

items.speaker: Medical Staff I
items.text: Hey, Vertin!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Hello.

items.speaker: Medical Staff I
items.text: Your friend is waiting for you in the rehab center. Mesmer Jr., remember?

items.speaker: Medical Staff II
items.text: Let us take you there, so you guys can catch up.
TO BE CONTINUED…
